title: Tan pronto como: la rapidez del contagio

sections.content: Tan pronto como (as soon as) stresses how immediately one event followed another -- the natural connector for a reading about how fast a New York stock crash became a Chilean export collapse. With a completed past event, it takes the indicative. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Tan pronto como la crisis financiera estadounidense comenzó a extenderse por el mundo, América Latina descubrió su vulnerabilidad estructural.
items.english: As soon as the American financial crisis began spreading around the world, Latin America discovered its structural vulnerability.

items.spanish: Tan pronto como la demanda mundial de café, cobre y salitre se desplomó, los precios de estos productos cayeron en picado.
items.english: As soon as world demand for coffee, copper and nitrates collapsed, the prices of these products plummeted.

items.spanish: Tan pronto como los bancos estadounidenses y europeos dejaron de prestar dinero, varios gobiernos se vieron obligados a suspender el pago de su deuda externa.
items.english: As soon as American and European banks stopped lending money, several governments were forced to suspend payment on their foreign debt.

items.spanish: Tan pronto como los gobiernos comprendieron la magnitud de lo que estaba ocurriendo, quedó claro que el modelo exportador no podría sobrevivir sin cambios.
items.english: As soon as governments understood the scale of what was happening, it became clear the export model couldn't survive without changes.

sections.content: Tan pronto como takes the subjunctive only when it refers to a future event that hasn't happened yet (tan pronto como lleguen, avísame) -- for a narrated sequence of past events, like this whole reading, the indicative is correct throughout.
